mainTopic: Weddings on ערב הרגל, the source for אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה, and the dedication of שלמה's מקדש
overview: A ברייתא allows weddings on ערב הרגל. The גמרא shows this fits all three reasons for banning weddings on חול המועד: the main joy and the main work are only on the wedding day, and nobody delays his wedding for just one day. Next the גמרא looks for the source of אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה. It first tries to prove it from שלמה keeping the dedication of the בית המקדש separate from סוכות, but that proof is rejected. The real source turns out to be the extra words 'seven days and seven days' in the פסוק. That celebration went through יום הכיפורים, and the people relied on a קל וחומר from the משכן, whose offerings were brought even on שבת. The גמרא proves the משכן point from the double 'day' wording in two פסוקים, and carries it over to the מקדש. A פסוק shows that ישראל were forgiven, and that the gates of the מקדש opened only in דוד's merit, proving he was forgiven too. The amud ends with students of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who learn from שלמה that a student must take leave of his teacher again. They then resolve a contradiction in משלי, and that answer finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Marrying right before the festival seems to clash with every reason
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows marrying on ערב הרגל, and the גמרא says this is a problem for all three reasons given for banning weddings on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The ברייתא says everyone] may marry on the day before the festival. This is a difficulty for all the opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that allows weddings on ערב הרגל, then says it seems to contradict every one of the three reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding celebration normally lasts seven days, so a wedding on ערב הרגל spills into the festival. The joy mixes, the work continues into the festival, and people might wait for this date to save money. So each reason should have forbidden it.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before a pilgrimage festival
It is difficult for all of them (all the opinions)

phrases.english: are permitted to marry on the eve of the festival,
This is difficult for all of them.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all three reasons given earlier for not marrying on חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three reasons from the previous page using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: All three reasons for banning weddings on חול המועד: שמחה, טירחא, and ביטול פריה ורביה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wedding on ערב הרגל carries its seven days of celebration into the festival, so each reason should forbid it, yet the ברייתא permits it.

steps.title: Answer for the joy reason: the main joy is only one day
steps.stepSummary: For the opinion that the ban is because of mixing joys, the main wedding joy is only the first day, which falls before the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. According to the one who says the reason is joy, the main joy is only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question, beginning with the reason of mixing joys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a wedding is celebrated for seven days, its main joy is the wedding day itself. If that day is ערב הרגל, the main wedding joy is over before the festival begins, so the two joys do not really mix.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
According to the one who says it is because of joy,
the main joy is only one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge for the first reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the concern: only the main day counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All seven days of wedding joy would mix with the festival.
steps.terutzMaskana: The main joy is only the wedding day, which falls before the festival.

steps.title: Answer for the work reason: the main work is only one day
steps.stepSummary: For the opinion that the ban is because of the work involved, the main work happens on the wedding day, before the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the reason is the work, the main work is only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for the second reason, the extra work a wedding brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavy preparations are for the wedding day itself. Once that day, ערב הרגל, has passed, no major work spills into the festival.

phrases.english: According to the one who says it is because of the exertion,
the main exertion is only one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same style of answer as step 2, applied to the second reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the concern: only the main day counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The work of the wedding would continue into the festival.
steps.terutzMaskana: The main work is done on the wedding day, before the festival.

steps.title: Answer for the פריה ורביה reason: no one waits for just one day
steps.stepSummary: For the opinion that the ban is to keep people from delaying marriage, nobody will hold off his wedding just to catch one particular day.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the reason is ביטול פריה ורביה, a person will not hold himself back for just one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question for the third reason and finishes its defense of all three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about חול המועד was that people would put off marrying to use the festival meals for the wedding too. A single day like ערב הרגל is not attractive enough for anyone to wait for, so there is no reason to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding off the מצוה of having children

steps.whatToRemember: Weddings on ערב הרגל are allowed according to all three reasons. The joy and the work are mainly on the one wedding day, and nobody delays marrying just to catch one day.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
phrases.english: According to the one who says it is because of neglecting being fruitful and multiplying,

phrases.aramaic: לְחַד יוֹמָא לָא מַשְׁהֵי אִינִישׁ נַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: a person will not hold himself back for just one day.
phrases.notes: He means nobody will push off his wedding just to land on this one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes answering the challenge for the third reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People would delay their weddings until ערב הרגל.
steps.terutzMaskana: No one delays a wedding for the sake of only one day.

steps.title: Where do we learn not to mix one joy with another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that we do not mix one joy with another, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks for the source of the joy rule. It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the rule אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה was used as a reason. Now the גמרא wants to know what it is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not mix one joy with another joy
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And that we do not mix joy with joy, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the joy reason from step 2 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה

steps.title: The פסוק about שלמה celebrating fourteen days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing שלמה's celebration as seven days and another seven days, fourteen days in all.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And שלמה held the festival at that time, and all ישראל with him, a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before ה׳ our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source. The reasoning from it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that the פסוק counts two separate sets of seven days. The first seven were for the dedication of the בית המקדש, and the second seven were סוכות.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Solomon held at that time
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:65

phrases.english: the festival, and all Israel with him,
a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath
to the Brook of Egypt, [before ה׳ our God,]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added here so the line matches the full פסוק.

phrases.english: seven days and seven days,
fourteen days."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיַּעַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹה בָעֵת הַהִיא אֶת הֶחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about שלמה's two separate seven-day celebrations

steps.title: Why שלמה didn't combine the two celebrations
steps.stepSummary: If mixing joys were allowed, שלמה should have waited for סוכות and made one seven-day celebration for both. Since he didn't, mixing joys is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were true that we may mix joy with joy, he should have waited until the festival and made seven days for this and for that together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה could have waited and held one seven-day celebration for both the dedication and סוכות. He held two separate weeks instead, which shows that one joy may not be mixed with another.
steps.whatToRemember: This first proof uses what שלמה did: he kept the dedication of the בית המקדש and סוכות as two separate weeks. Steps 8–12 challenge this proof, and step 13 gives the source that holds up: the extra words in the פסוק.

phrases.english: And if it were so that we may mix joy with joy,
he should have waited until the festival,
phrases.notes: "The festival" here is סוכות, the second set of seven days.

phrases.english: and made seven days for this and for that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reasoning out of the פסוק quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שלמה held two separate seven-day celebrations instead of combining the dedication with סוכות (מלכים א 8:65)

steps.title: Maybe we only don't wait for a festival on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof from שלמה. Maybe it only teaches that we don't delay a celebration so it lands on a יום טוב. If it happens to land there on its own, we may celebrate both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe we just don't wait for the festival on purpose, and when the two happen to fall together, we do celebrate them together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 7. It says שלמה's behavior might show something smaller than a full ban on mixing joys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה finished the בית המקדש before סוכות and did not hold off the celebration. That may only prove you shouldn't delay a joy to make it overlap with a festival. It does not prove that two joys which fall together by chance must be kept apart.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not saying mixing joys is allowed in general. It only says the proof from שלמה might be limited to deliberately waiting.

phrases.english: But perhaps we just do not wait for it,
phrases.notes: He means we don't push off a celebration on purpose so it lands on the festival.

phrases.english: but where it happens that way on its own, we do celebrate together!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from שלמה's separate celebrations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה's behavior only shows not delaying on purpose. It does not show that joys falling together by chance are forbidden.

steps.title: He could have left a little of the building unfinished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the proof. If combining joys were allowed, שלמה could have left a small part of the building undone until סוכות. Then the celebrations would have fallen together naturally.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have left a little bit unfinished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שלמה had a simple way to make the two joys come together without openly waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a small piece unfinished would have let the dedication land on סוכות. Since שלמה didn't do that, it seems combining joys really is forbidden.

phrases.english: He should have left a little bit unfinished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing an available alternative that שלמה did not use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה only avoided deliberately waiting for סוכות
steps.terutzMaskana: He could have made the joys meet by leaving part of the work undone, and he didn't

steps.title: You may not leave the בית המקדש unfinished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. It is not allowed to leave any part of the building of the בית המקדש undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not leave any part of the building of the בית המקדש unfinished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 9. שלמה had no right to leave part of the building undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה's not leaving a piece unfinished proves nothing. He couldn't have done it anyway, so the challenge of step 8 comes back.

phrases.english: Leaving part of the building of the Temple unfinished
is something we do not do.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁיּוֹרֵי בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לָא מְשַׁיְּירִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that שלמה could have left part of the building undone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Leaving the בית המקדש building unfinished is not allowed

steps.title: He could have left the raven spikes unfinished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again. שלמה could have left the spiked plates that keep ravens off the roof until later. Those don't seem to be part of the actual building.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have left the cubit-wide raven guard unfinished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to save the proof. It points to a small extra that is not really part of the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the raven spikes are only an add-on, leaving them for later would not break the rule of step 10. Then שלמה could have pushed off the dedication until סוכות, and he didn't.

keyTerms.meaning: The cubit-wide spikes that keep ravens away

phrases.english: He should have left unfinished
the cubit that keeps away the ravens.
phrases.notes: These were sharp metal spikes on the roof that kept ravens from landing there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְשַׁיּוֹרֵי בְּאַמָּה כָּלְיָא עוֹרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer the challenge of step 8, after step 10 rejected the first
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a non-structural part that could have been delayed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing at all could be left unfinished
steps.terutzMaskana: The raven spikes could have been delayed without leaving the building itself unfinished

steps.title: The raven spikes are part of the building too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this too. The raven spikes were a necessary part of the בית המקדש building.
steps.simpleTranslation: The raven guard is a needed part of the building of the House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second answer. The raven spikes also count as part of the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the spikes are a building need, the rule from step 10 covers them too. So the proof from שלמה's actions fails completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A need of the building of the House (the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: The cubit that keeps away the ravens
is a needed part of the building of the House.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמָּה כָּלְיָא עוֹרֵב צוֹרֶךְ בִּנְיַן הַבַּיִת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof built on what שלמה did
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The raven spikes are also part of the building, so they could not be left undone

steps.title: The real proof comes from the extra words in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof. The פסוק already says fourteen days. So why does it also say seven days and seven days? It teaches that each set of seven must stand on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from the extra words in the פסוק. Since it says 'fourteen days,' why do I need 'seven days and seven days'? Learn from this that these are separate and those are separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the proof from שלמה's actions. It proves the rule from the wording of the פסוק instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'fourteen days' already give the total, so splitting it into 'seven and seven' would be extra. The extra words teach that the dedication celebration and סוכות must each be kept separate. That is exactly אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the פסוק has extra words

steps.whatToRemember: The source for אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה is the extra words 'seven days and seven days' in the פסוק, not what שלמה chose to do.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof stands no matter how the building schedule worked, so the rule now has a firm source.

phrases.english: Rather, the proof is from the fact that the verse has extra words:
since it is written "fourteen days,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:65

phrases.english: why do I need "seven days and seven days"?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הָנֵי לְחוֹד וְהָנֵי לְחוֹד.
phrases.english: Learn from it: these are separate and those are separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new one from the פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The rule אין מערבין שמחה בשמחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'seven days and seven days' next to 'fourteen days' in the פסוק

steps.title: That year ישראל did not keep יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרנך quotes רבי יוחנן. In the year of the dedication, ישראל did not keep יום הכיפורים. The people worried they might deserve destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרנך said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That year, ישראל did not keep יום הכיפורים. They were worried and said: Maybe ישראל have become deserving of destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a story about שלמה's celebration. It sets up the people's worry, which gets answered in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven days of celebration included יום הכיפורים, so the people ate and feasted that day. They feared this was a sin deserving destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: The enemies of ישראל (a polite way of saying ישראל themselves)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Parnakh said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
That year the Jewish people did not observe
Yom Kippur.
And they were worried and said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא נִתְחַיְּיבוּ שׂוֹנְאֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָיָיה,
phrases.english: Perhaps the enemies of Israel have become liable to destruction,
phrases.notes: "Enemies of Israel" is a polite way of saying the Jewish people themselves, so as not to say something bad about them directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי פַּרְנָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related story about the same celebration of שלמה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the year of the dedication, ישראל did not keep יום הכיפורים, and they feared punishment

steps.title: A בת קול promises them עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A heavenly voice answered the people's worry. It told them they were all destined for the World to Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said to them: All of you are ready for life in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a heavenly voice that answers the people's fear from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of being punished for feasting on יום הכיפורים, the people were promised עולם הבא. This shows their celebration of the בית המקדש was accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Life in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: Even though they did not keep יום הכיפורים during the dedication, the people were promised עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A Divine Voice came out and said to them:
All of you are destined for life in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were not punished. They were all promised life in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What reasoning did the people use?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what line of thinking led the people to eat on יום הכיפורים during the dedication.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they learn out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what reasoning the people used to allow themselves to eat on יום הכיפורים. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said they did not keep יום הכיפורים, and they were not simply careless. The גמרא wants to know what logic they relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they learn out / what was their reasoning?

phrases.english: What did they derive?
phrases.notes: He means: what reasoning made them think eating on יום הכיפורים was allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the behavior described in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical basis the people used to eat on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The people reasoned that if the משכן's dedication pushed aside שבת, the מקדש's dedication can surely push aside יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: a קל וחומר. The משכן's holiness was not permanent, yet a single person's offering pushed aside שבת, which carries סקילה. The מקדש's holiness is permanent, its offerings were for the whole community, and יום הכיפורים only carries כרת. Surely it can push aside יום הכיפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people used a קל וחומר, comparing the dedication of the משכן to the dedication of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three points of comparison. The משכן was temporary, while the מקדש was permanent. The משכן had a קרבן יחיד, each נשיא's own offering, while the מקדש had a קרבן ציבור. שבת carries the harsher punishment of סקילה, while יום הכיפורים carries כרת. On every point the מקדש case is stronger, so they concluded it surely overrides יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one
An offering of the whole community
Stoning, the punishment for breaking שבת
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating on יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: They said: an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מִשְׁכָּן, שֶׁאֵין קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת עוֹלָם —
phrases.english: If the Tabernacle, whose holiness is not permanent holiness,

phrases.aramaic: וְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת דְּאִיסּוּר סְקִילָה,
phrases.english: and an individual's offering overrides Shabbat, a prohibition punished by stoning,
phrases.notes: The 'individual' here is each tribal leader (נשיא), who brought his own offering at the משכן.

phrases.aramaic: מִקְדָּשׁ, דִּקְדוּשָּׁתוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת עוֹלָם, וְקׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: then the Temple, whose holiness is permanent, and with a communal offering,
and Yom Kippur, which is punished only by karet,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the משכן overriding שבת to the מקדש overriding יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Then why were they worried?
steps.stepSummary: If they had such a strong argument, why were they afraid they deserved punishment?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, why were they worried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If the people had a solid קל וחומר, why did they fear they deserved destruction?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 described their worry, and step 17 gave them a strong reason. The two do not seem to fit together, so the גמרא is pointing out the tension.

phrases.english: But then why were they worried?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how strong the קל וחומר in step 17 really was.
steps.kashyaTarget: The people's worry in step 14 compared with the strong reasoning in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A good proof should have removed their fear, yet they were still afraid.

steps.title: Heaven's need versus human need
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר had a weak point. The משכן broke שבת for Heaven's needs, while eating is a human need.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was for Heaven's need. Here, it was for a human need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the קל וחומר could be challenged, and that is why they were worried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the משכן, שבת was pushed aside only to bring offerings, which is צורך גבוה. At the מקדש they ate and drank, which is a צורך הדיוט. That difference weakens the comparison and explains their fear.

keyTerms.meaning: A need of Heaven, such as offerings
An ordinary human need, such as eating

phrases.english: There, it was a need of the One on High;
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משכן; 'here' in the next line is the מקדש.

phrases.english: here, it was an ordinary person's need.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם צוֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ, הָכָא צוֹרֶךְ הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by finding a weak point in the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It could be challenged, since eating is a human need, so the worry made sense.

steps.title: So they should have skipped the eating
steps.stepSummary: If eating is only a human need, they should have brought the offerings and fasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, they should have done the service, but not eaten or drunk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If only the offerings were justified, why didn't they just bring the offerings and still fast?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19's distinction seems to suggest an easy fix. They could keep the Heavenly part of the dedication and drop the eating. So why did they eat at all?

keyTerms.meaning: They should certainly do the service

phrases.english: Here too: let them do the service,
but let them not eat and not drink!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 19's distinction to question why they ate at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: Their decision to eat and drink on יום הכיפורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the offerings were justified, they could have brought them and still fasted.

steps.title: No celebration without food and drink
steps.stepSummary: Eating was needed because there is no real שמחה without eating and drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no rejoicing without eating and drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eating was part of the celebration of the dedication itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dedication called for שמחה, and real שמחה needs eating and drinking. So the eating was tied to the dedication, but it was still a human need, which is why they stayed worried.
steps.whatToRemember: The people relied on a קל וחומר from the משכן. They still worried because eating is a human need, but it was necessary for the שמחה of the dedication.

phrases.english: There is no rejoicing without eating and drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the eating was necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating was optional and could have been skipped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating was part of the required שמחה of the dedication.

steps.title: How do we know the משכן offerings overrode שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the dedication offerings at the משכן were brought on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that the משכן overrode שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the starting point of the קל וחומר. Where do we see that the משכן offerings pushed aside שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole קל וחומר in step 17 depends on this fact. If it is not proven, the argument falls apart.

phrases.english: And the Tabernacle overriding Shabbat, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to check the base of step 17's קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the משכן dedication offerings were brought on שבת.

steps.title: The first proof: the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: A first proof from 'the seventh day' is suggested and turned down, since it could mean the seventh day of offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is from the verses 'on the first day' and 'on the seventh day,' maybe it means the seventh day of offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible proof and immediately turns it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the נשיאים brought offerings for twelve days, one of those days must have been שבת, and 'the seventh day' might seem to be שבת. But it could just mean the seventh offering day, and they may have skipped שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The seventh day' here does not have to mean שבת. It can just mean the seventh in the count of offering days.

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"On the first day," and "on the seventh day,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:12 and 7:48.

phrases.english: perhaps it means the seventh day of the offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests and then rejects a first answer to step 22.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Seventh' could count offering days, not days of the week.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: one continuous stretch
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves from 'on the day of the eleventh day' that the offering days ran without a break.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The verse says 'on the day of the eleventh day.' Just as a day is all one continuous stretch, so too the eleven days were all continuous.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a better proof from the extra word 'day' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word 'day' links the eleven days to a single day. A single day has no gaps, so the eleven days had no gaps either, not even for שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The verse states: "On the day of the eleventh day."
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:72.

phrases.english: Just as a day is entirely continuous,
so too, the eleven were all continuous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That the משכן offerings continued through שבת.

steps.title: Maybe only the suitable days
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the eleven continuous days only counted days fit for offerings, leaving out שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it means the days that are fit for offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Continuous' might mean continuous among the days that were fit for a קרבן יחיד. Then שבת could have been skipped without breaking the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: Days that are fit for these offerings

phrases.english: But perhaps it means the fitting days?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe they counted only weekdays, skipping שבת, and still called it continuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from 'continuous'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Continuity could mean only among the days that were fit for offerings, which leaves out שבת.

steps.title: A second verse: the twelfth day
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק, 'on the day of the twelfth day,' repeats the pattern and confirms that all the days were continuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: 'On the day of the twelfth day.' Just as a day is all continuous, so too the twelve days were all continuous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a second פסוק that has the same 'day... day' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק has the same 'day... day' wording, so it suggests that all twelve days ran straight through, including שבת. The next step questions whether this פסוק could also mean only fitting days, and step 28 settles it.
steps.whatToRemember: The משכן offerings of the נשיאים ran for twelve days in a row, including שבת. That is the base of the קל וחומר for the מקדש dedication.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"On the day of the twelfth day."
phrases.notes: במדבר 7:78.

phrases.english: Just as a day is entirely continuous,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם כּוּלָּן רְצוּפִין.
phrases.english: so too, the twelve days were all continuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 with an additional פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The days might have been continuous only among suitable days, skipping שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second 'day... day' פסוק confirms that all twelve days were truly continuous, including שבת.

steps.title: Maybe the twelfth day also counts only fitting days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the 'twelfth day' פסוק might also count only days fit for offerings, leaving out שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe here too, it means only the days that are fit for offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the 'twelfth day' פסוק in Step 26. Maybe that פסוק also counts only the days that were fit for offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 used a second פסוק to show the days ran without a break. The same doubt from Step 25 can be raised again: maybe this פסוק also skips שבת and counts only fitting days. If so, the second פסוק adds nothing new.

phrases.english: But perhaps here too
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the 'twelfth day' פסוק from the last step.

phrases.english: it means days that are fit (for offerings)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 26 by repeating the doubt from Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'on the day of the twelfth day' in Step 26
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'only fitting days' reading that weakened the first פסוק could apply to the second one too.

steps.title: Two verses would not be needed for the same point
steps.stepSummary: If both פסוקים meant only 'fitting days,' the Torah would not need two of them. So they teach that the days were continuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need two verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the Torah would not write two פסוקים just to say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'fitting days' were the meaning, one פסוק would be enough. Having a second one shows it teaches something extra: the days really ran straight through, including שבת. So the proof from Step 26 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The dedication offerings of the משכן were brought every day in a row, even on שבת. We know this because the Torah repeats the 'on the day of' wording in two פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need two verses?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-verse argument (a repeated פסוק must teach something new)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים might count only the days fit for offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two פסוקים prove the days were continuous, including שבת.

steps.title: Source that the מקדש celebration overrode יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the celebration at the dedication of the מקדש pushed aside יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the מקדש dedication, which pushed aside יום הכיפורים, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. How do we know the dedication of שלמה's מקדש went on right through יום הכיפורים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the משכן dedication ran through שבת, the גמרא asks a matching question about the מקדש. There the celebrating and eating went on even on יום הכיפורים. It wants a source for this.

phrases.english: And the Temple, which overrides Yom Kippur, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He means the feasting at the Temple's dedication, so the people did not fast that יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משכן and שבת to the parallel question about the מקדש and יום הכיפורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the מקדש dedication celebration continued through יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Fourteen days might mean only fitting days
steps.stepSummary: A first idea, the phrase 'fourteen days,' is turned down because it could mean only days fit for feasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from what is written, 'fourteen days,' maybe that means only days fit for feasting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first source, 'fourteen days,' and then right away knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fourteen days' might count only the days fit for celebrating and leave out יום הכיפורים. This is the same weakness we saw with the משכן. So this פסוק alone does not prove anything.

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"Fourteen days",
phrases.notes: מלכים א ח:סה

phrases.english: but perhaps it means days that are fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries and rejects a first answer to the question in Step 29.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The count could include only days fit for feasting and skip יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Learned from 'day' and 'day' at the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'day' here is compared to the word 'day' by the משכן, where the days were proven to be continuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'day' 'day' from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. It uses a word comparison: 'day' in the מקדש story matches 'day' in the משכן story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the משכן we already proved, with two פסוקים, that the days ran without a break. Since the same word 'day' shows up by the מקדש, the same rule carries over. So there too the days were continuous, even through יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatToRemember: The מקדש celebration ran through יום הכיפורים. We know this by comparing the word 'day' to the משכן, where the days ran through שבת.

phrases.english: He derives "day" "day" from there.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משכן dedication, where we just proved the days ran without a break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real source after Step 30 rejected the first try.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A word comparison of 'day' to the משכן shows the מקדש days were continuous too.

steps.title: How do we know they were forgiven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the בת קול that promised everyone עולם הבא, and asks how we know they were forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said to them: All of you are set for life in the World to Come. And from where do we know that He forgave them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line said earlier, the בת קול. It asks for a source that the people were forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the story said a בת קול promised them עולם הבא. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק showing that ה׳ really forgave them for not fasting on יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Life in the World to Come

phrases.english: A heavenly voice went out and said to them:
All of you are set for life in the World to Come.
And from where do we know that He forgave them?
phrases.notes: Forgave them for eating and celebrating on יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story of the מקדש dedication and asks for a source for the forgiveness.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing ה׳ forgave the people for not fasting on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: תחליפא quotes the verse about the people going home
steps.stepSummary: תחליפא teaches a פסוק describing the people going home happy for all the good ה׳ did.
steps.simpleTranslation: As תחליפא taught: "On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king, and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that ה׳ had done for דוד His servant and for ישראל His people."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא from תחליפא. He cites the פסוק that will show they were forgiven, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the people leaving the dedication full of joy. On its own it does not openly say they were forgiven. The proof comes when each phrase is explained in the next step.

phrases.english: As Tachlifa taught:
"On the eighth day he sent the people away,
phrases.notes: מלכים א ח:סו

phrases.english: and they blessed the king,
and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל הַטּוֹבָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה ה׳
phrases.english: for all the goodness that ה׳ had done
for David His servant and for Israel His people."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in Step 32 by quoting the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in מלכים about the people going home joyful, explained in the next step.

steps.title: Each phrase of the verse explained, ending with the promise of the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: Each phrase of the פסוק is explained. 'For all the goodness' refers to the בת קול promising them עולם הבא, which proves they were forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: "To their tents": they went and found their wives pure. "Joyful": they enjoyed the shine of the Divine Presence. "Glad of heart": each one's wife became pregnant with a boy. "For all the goodness": a heavenly voice came out and told them, all of you are set for life in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes through the פסוק phrase by phrase. The last phrase, 'for all the goodness,' is what answers our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each joyful word in the פסוק is tied to a specific blessing. 'All the goodness' is read as the greatest good of all, the promise of עולם הבא. Someone promised עולם הבא was clearly forgiven, so this proves ה׳ pardoned them.

keyTerms.meaning: The shine of the Divine Presence

steps.whatToRemember: The people at the dedication of the מקדש did not fast on יום הכיפורים, and they were fully forgiven. 'For all the goodness' teaches that a בת קול promised all of them עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The forgiveness is not stated outright in the פסוק. It comes only from the last phrase, 'for all the goodness,' read as the promise of עולם הבא. The other phrases list extra blessings.

phrases.english: "To their tents": that they went
and found their wives in purity,
"Joyful": that they enjoyed the shine of the Divine Presence,
"And glad of heart": that each and every one,
his wife became pregnant with a male child,
"For all the goodness": that a heavenly voice went out
and said to them: All of you are set
for life in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in Step 33 and finishes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ forgave the people for not fasting on יום הכיפורים
steps.raayaSupportSource: תחליפא's reading of 'for all the goodness' in מלכים א ח:סו as the בת קול's promise of עולם הבא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone at the dedication of the מקדש was forgiven and promised עולם הבא.

steps.title: What good was done for דוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the פסוק. It understands 'for Israel His people,' but asks what 'for David His servant' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'For David His servant and for Israel His people.' We understand 'for Israel His people': ה׳ forgave them for eating on יום הכיפורים. But what good did ה׳ do 'for David His servant'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still on the same פסוק and now asks about its last phrase. Half of it is already clear, and the other half needs an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good done for ישראל was already explained in the earlier steps: forgiveness for not fasting on יום הכיפורים. But דוד had already passed away before the חנוכת הבית, so the גמרא wants to know what good was done for him at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introducing the part that is hard)
The sin of not fasting on יום כיפור

phrases.english: "For David His servant and for Israel His people."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק from the last step (מלכים א 8:66).

phrases.english: Granted, "for Israel His people"
means that He forgave them the sin of Yom Kippur,
but "for David His servant," what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק phrase by phrase, now reaching its last words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What goodness ה׳ showed to דוד at the dedication of the מקדש.

steps.title: The gates of the מקדש would not open for שלמה
steps.stepSummary: רב tells that when שלמה tried to bring the ארון into the מקדש, the gates stuck together. His many songs and prayers did not open them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When שלמה wanted to bring the ארון into the מקדש, the gates stuck to each other. שלמה said twenty-four songs of praise and was not answered. He began saying 'Lift up your heads, O gates' and was still not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב begins his answer with a story. This part sets up the problem, the stuck gates, and the next step shows how it was solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that even שלמה's own great prayers were not enough to open the gates. This makes it stand out when they finally do open, so we see clearly whose merit opened them.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At the time that Solomon wanted
to bring the Ark into the Temple,
the gates stuck to each other.
Solomon said twenty-four songs of praise
and was not answered.
He began and said: "Lift up your heads, O gates, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:7

phrases.english: and was still not answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question about דוד.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A story that leads to showing דוד's forgiveness. This part sets up the stuck gates.

steps.title: Mentioning דוד opens the gates and shows he was forgiven
steps.stepSummary: As soon as שלמה asked ה׳ to remember the kindness of דוד, the gates opened. Everyone saw that ה׳ had forgiven דוד for his sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שלמה said, 'ה׳, do not turn away the face of Your anointed one; remember the kindness of דוד Your servant,' he was answered right away. At that moment, the faces of דוד's enemies turned dark like the bottom of a pot. Everyone knew that ה׳ had forgiven דוד for that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the gates open only in the merit of דוד. This answers the question: the good done for דוד was showing the world that he was forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's enemies had claimed that his sin was never forgiven. When the gates opened only because of his merit, it proved in public that ה׳ accepted him. That is the 'goodness for David His servant' in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the bottom of a pot (blackened)

steps.whatToRemember: 'For David His servant' means ה׳ showed everyone that דוד was forgiven, because the gates of the מקדש opened only in his merit.

phrases.english: Once he said:
"O Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed;
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 6:42

phrases.english: remember the kindnesses of David Your servant,"
he was answered right away.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נֶהְפְּכוּ פְּנֵי שׂוֹנְאֵי דָוִד
phrases.english: At that moment the faces of David's enemies turned
like the bottom of a pot,
phrases.notes: The bottom of a cooking pot is black from the fire, so their faces darkened with shame.

phrases.english: and everyone knew
that the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgave him
for that sin.
phrases.notes: 'That sin' is the well-known sin of דוד with בת שבע.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר ״ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אַל תָּשֵׁב פְּנֵי מְשִׁיחֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's story and shows how it answers the question.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'goodness for David His servant' was the public sign of his forgiveness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The gates opened only when דוד's merit was mentioned, and his enemies were shamed.

steps.title: Two students take leave of רבי שמעון בן יוחי twice
steps.stepSummary: A new story: two students learned with רבי שמעון בן יוחי, said goodbye in the evening, and came back to say goodbye again in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן בן עסמאי and רבי יהודה בן גרים learned the section of vows in the house of רבי שמעון בן יוחי. They took leave of him in the evening. In the morning they came back and took leave of him again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand new story. This part sets the scene for what רבי שמעון בן יוחי will say to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students said goodbye at night but did not leave town yet, so in the morning they said goodbye again. This double goodbye is what makes their רבי ask them a question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The section of the תורה about vows

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַסְמַיי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גֵּרִים
phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Asmai and Rabbi Yehuda, son of converts,
studied the section of vows
in the house of study of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.
They took leave of him in the evening.
In the morning they came back and were taking leave of him again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַסְמַיי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן גֵּרִים תָּנוּ פָּרָשַׁת נְדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after finishing the topic of דוד's forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two students took leave of their רבי twice, once at night and again in the morning.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks why they said goodbye again
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks the students why they are saying goodbye again, since they already did so the night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Didn't you already take leave of me in the evening?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks the students a question. This sets up their answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He notices the second goodbye and wants to know the reason for it. The story will continue with the students' answer and what happened after.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't you? (asking about something that already happened)

phrases.english: He said to them:
Didn't you already take leave of me in the evening?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: וְלָאו אִיפַּטְרִיתוּ מִינַּי בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new story with רבי שמעון's question about the second goodbye.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the students came back to take leave a second time.

steps.title: The students explain why they came back to say goodbye
steps.stepSummary: The students remind רבי שמעון בן יוחי of his own teaching: a student who says goodbye and then sleeps in the same city must say goodbye again. The source is two פסוקים about the day שלמה sent the people home.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You taught us, our rebbe, that a student who says goodbye to his teacher and then sleeps over in that same city must say goodbye to him another time. As the פסוק says: 'On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king.' And another פסוק says: 'And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away'!
steps.whatsHappening: The students answer the question from step 39. They are only doing what רבי שמעון בן יוחי himself taught them, and they quote his source from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says שלמה sent the people away on the eighth day, which is שמיני עצרת, the 22nd of תשרי. Another פסוק says he sent them away on the 23rd. The two dates set up the proof that they said goodbye twice, and that proof is spelled out in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to him: You taught us, our rebbe,
that a student who says goodbye to his teacher
and then sleeps over in that same city
must say goodbye to him another time,
as it says: 'On the eighth day he sent the people away,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:66. The 'eighth day' is שמיני עצרת, the 22nd of תשרי.

phrases.english: and they blessed the king,'
and it is written: 'And on the twenty-third day
of the seventh month he sent the people away'!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 7:10. This is one day later than the first פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי שמעון בן יוחי asked in step 39.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the students come back to say goodbye a second time?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They followed his own teaching that a student who sleeps over in the same city must say goodbye again, based on two פסוקים about שלמה.

steps.title: The two dates prove a second goodbye is needed
steps.stepSummary: The only way to fit the two פסוקים together is that the people said goodbye on the 22nd, slept over, and said goodbye again on the 23rd. So a student who sleeps in the same city must say goodbye again.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it must be that we learn from here: a student who says goodbye to his teacher and then sleeps over in that same city must say goodbye to him another time.
steps.whatsHappening: The students finish their proof. They draw the rule out of the two different dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people were sent away on the 22nd, but they stayed overnight in ירושלים. So on the 23rd they were sent away again, which means they took leave of שלמה a second time. A student who sleeps over in his teacher's city should do the same.
steps.whatToRemember: A student who says goodbye to his rebbe and then stays the night in the same city must say goodbye again, learned from the two dates on which שלמה sent the people home.

phrases.english: So it must be, from here we learn
about a student who says goodbye to his teacher
and then sleeps over in that same city,
that he must say goodbye to him another time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the rule out of the two פסוקים quoted in step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A student who sleeps over in the same city after saying goodbye must say goodbye again.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי sends his son to get a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי tells his son that these two students are great people and that he should go to them for a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his son: These people are men of great stature. Go to them so that they will bless you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. רבי שמעון בן יוחי praises the students and sends his son to them, which sets up the next scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling them 'men of צורה' means they are wise and learned. Because of that, a ברכה from them is worth getting.

keyTerms.meaning: people of great stature (wise and learned)
so that they will bless you

phrases.english: He said to his son:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שמעון בן יוחי.

phrases.english: These people
are men of great stature,
phrases.notes: Literally 'men of form.' He means they are wise, distinguished תלמידי חכמים.

phrases.english: go to them so that they will bless you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the two students after their explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן יוחי sends his son to get a ברכה from the two great students.

steps.title: Two פסוקים in משלי seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The son finds the students pointing out a contradiction. One פסוק says to weigh your path carefully, and another says not to weigh the path of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found them raising contradictions between פסוקים. It is written: 'Weigh the path of your feet, and all your ways will be firm.' And it is written: 'Lest you weigh the path of life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The son arrives and finds the students busy with a question. They point out that two פסוקים in משלי seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says to 'weigh' your path, meaning you should figure out which מצוה is more important. The second פסוק says not to weigh the path of life, meaning you should just do each מצוה as it comes. These two ideas seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: weigh, measure out (like on a scale)

phrases.english: He went, and found them
pointing out contradictions between פסוקים.
It is written: 'Weigh the path of your feet,
phrases.notes: משלי 4:26. This sounds like: compare which מצוה is more important.

phrases.english: and all your ways will be firm,'
and it is written: 'Lest you weigh the path of life.'
phrases.notes: משלי 5:6. This sounds like: don't compare, just do each מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל, אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא רָמוּ קְרָאֵי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The son reaches the students and finds them discussing a new question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים in משלי 4:26 and 5:6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says to weigh which path or מצוה to choose, and the other says not to weigh. They seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: The first פסוק is about a מצוה others can do
steps.stepSummary: The students start to resolve the contradiction. The פסוק that says to weigh is talking about a מצוה that other people can do instead of you.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem: here, it is talking about a מצוה that can be done by others.
steps.whatsHappening: The students begin answering the contradiction. They explain the first case, and the second half of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone else can do the מצוה, you should weigh which one is more important for you to do yourself and leave the rest to others. This explains 'weigh the path of your feet.' The other פסוק is explained at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: It is not a problem:
here, it is talking about a מצוה
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the first פסוק, 'weigh the path of your feet.'

phrases.english: that can be done by others,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּמִצְוָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the contradiction raised in step 43.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק is talking about a different kind of מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seemed to give opposite instructions for the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק that says to weigh is about a מצוה others can do. The other case continues on the next amud.
